title: Company Objective Fabric: initiative bundling, release pacing, and contingency crediting
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: As company-level OKRs proliferate, teams are independently launching initiatives that overlap in customer signal, infra consumption, and release timing. This causes noisy rollouts, contested GPU/reserved capacity, and opaque progress against company outcomes.

Goal: Create a lightweight operational model (the "Objective Fabric") that groups related initiatives into delivery bundles tied to a single company OKR outcome, prescribes release pacing windows, and establishes a contingency credit pool to reallocate capacity without breaking SLAs. The Fabric should reduce release collisions by 60% and improve cross-team visibility for the exec dashboard.

Scope: Cross-functional playbook + lightweight tooling/labels in Linear and Console to: bundle initiatives, assign a delivery pace (fast/steady/pulse), declare a contingency credit amount, and define escalation lanes. Bundles can span Product, Eng, Design, and Solutions. We will prototype with 3 OKRs and ~12 initiatives in Q2.

What success looks like:
- Release collisions (two or more initiatives seeking same Dedicated capacity window) reduced by 60% vs baseline.
- 75% of bundle owners actively using the Fabric labels and a central dashboard link.
- Contingency credit pool used to resolve at least 2 capacity conflicts without delaying customer-impacting work.

Out-of-scope: Automated capacity provisioning or infra implementation details. We will not change Dedicated autoscaling behavior in this ticket; ENG follow-ups will own infra changes.

High-level approach:
1) Define the bundle schema and minimal metadata fields (OKR id, primary outcome, owners, delivery pace, contingency_credit, gating_criteria, escalation_path). These will be encoded as labels + a short descriptor in Linear ticket titles.
2) Run a 3-week pilot with 3 OKRs: onboarding latency, cost-per-token, and rollout reliability. Gather telemetry from Console dashboards and a small intake form for initiative owners.
3) Build a lightweight Fabric dashboard (Confluence + Console alias) that surfaces bundles, windows, and outstanding dependencies.
4) Iterate the acceptance criteria and operational playbook based on pilot feedback and the leadership sync.

Key trade-offs considered:
- Strict bundling reduces autonomy but improves predictability. We opt for soft-guardrails (labels + pacing windows) with a lightweight adjudication committee rather than hard gating.
- Contingency credits introduce complexity in capacity accounting; to limit scope, credits will be manual transfers tracked in a shared spreadsheet and reconciled monthly.

Links / artifacts:
- Pilot intake form: https://forms.redwood.ai/pilot-objective-fabric (prototype)
- Confluence playbook draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/Objective+Fabric+Playbook
- Prototype dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/okr-fabric-pilot
- Example bundle mapping spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ObjFabricExample
